Choose any of the thirteen; these four cards follow it.
Who wrote it, to whom, from where, when and why; who and where it names; its key verses and its themes.

Paul, writing as "a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle". No one shares the opening greeting, but the letter was taken down by a scribe who greets the readers in his own name, Tertius, the only scribe any of Paul's letters names. Seven companions add their greetings at the end. Romans 1:1 Romans 16:22 Romans 16:21–23

16For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek. 17For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith. Romans 1:16–17 · KJV
The thesis of the letter: the gospel is God's power to save, and "the just shall live by faith".
God's righteousness, revealed in the gospel and received by faith. Romans 1:17 Romans 3:21–26
Jew and Gentile alike are under sin. Romans 3:9 Romans 3:23
Justification by faith apart from the works of the law, with Abraham as the pattern. Romans 3:28 Romans 4:3
Adam and Christ as the two heads of humanity. Romans 5:12–21
Union with Christ in his death and resurrection, pictured in baptism. Romans 6:3–11
The Holy Spirit as the power of the new life. Romans 8:1–39
God's faithfulness to Israel, and the Gentiles grafted in. Romans 9:1–11:36
Love as the fulfilling of the law, and living together when consciences differ. Romans 13:8–10 Romans 14:1–15:7

Where the quotations in Paul's letters come from, book by book. Click a book or a letter to keep it. Below, each quotation in Romans, linked to the passage it comes from.

Each band joins an Old Testament book to a letter that quotes it; its width is the number of places in the letter that quote that book (a passage drawing on two verses of one book counts once). Allusions are left out. The lists are the dossiers' selection of clear quotations, not a census of every echo. Romans quotes far more than any other letter, above all from Isaiah and the Psalms; Habakkuk 2:4, Genesis 15:6, Leviticus 18:5 and Leviticus 19:18 are quoted in both Romans and Galatians. Romans 1:17 Galatians 3:11
